sekcje: Drug Levels and Effects > Summary of Use during Lactation

No information is available on the clinical use of bulevirtide during breastfeeding. Because bulevirtide is more than 99% bound to plasma proteins, has liver tropism, and high specificity for sodium taurocholate co-transporting polypeptide, the amount in milk is likely to be low. It is a peptide that is likely digested in the infant’s gastrointestinal tract, so it is unlikely to reach the clinically important levels in infant serum. If a mother requires bulevirtide, it is not a reason to discontinue breastfeeding.
